runs.text: The Kalal Idiga are a caste in India, traditionally known for

(tapping the sap from the Toddy tree in order to make alcohol). Because alcohol is looked down upon in Indian society, the Kalal Idiga are considered by others as low caste people. The government has classed the Kalal Idiga as a ‘Backward Class’, this allows them certain privileges such as allotted entry into universities but reflects their low status in society.

Recently, some of the Kalal Idiga have broken free from their traditional occupation and have entered the business world and even politics. However, many who still live in the countryside, continue to live from day to day in very poor conditions.

The southern states of Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana are home to many Kalal Idiga, though they can also be found in several other states in southern India. Some of these states have passed laws against changing one’s religion. Karnataka did pass such a law, but it has since been lifted.

The government in India strongly promotes Hinduism, which can lead to imprisonment of Christians who lead someone to Christ. Travel restrictions for locals and ex-pats can limit access to remote places where Kalal Idiga live, however, Indian Christians still go out to share the Gospel and some Kalal Idiga, mostly in towns and cities where churches are, have come to faith in Jesus.

The Kalal Idiga caste of India now have a population of just over 2 million. They are known for alcohol production and so are looked down upon by Hindu Society. Jesus came to set people like the Kalal Idiga free.
“Jesus said “The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to
, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised.”
Pray for the Kalal Idiga community, that they may experience freedom, healing, provision,
hope in the Gospel, and restored dignity through God’s love
Pray that many Kalal Idiga would come to know and trust Jesus as their Lord and Saviour.
Pray that God’s glory may be shown in the lives of Kalal Idiga Christians.
Pray that those Kalal Idiga who remain in alcohol production may be set free from the binds of the caste system and know that they can become children of God.
Pray for God given strategies to reach the Kalal Idiga and the communities that they live in.
